why: A district workforce of about 1.2 million split across earnings groups, employer sizes and contact levels is believable for a large urban district, and no subgroup exceeds its group.
All four pies sum to 100%, and 900 respondents being 18% of a campus of about 5,000 students is believable for a business school.
The cost bars add exactly to the €908 million total, and a regional airline with fuel at about 31% of operating costs is believable.
A water company serving 900,000 homes taking 320,000 calls from 105k callers (groups sum to 105k) at about £6.4m total cost is believable.
Contract fitter hours stay below total hours every week, and a near doubling of bookings and hours at the winter tyre changeover is believable.
Both the 100% stacked bar and the gym-goal pie sum to 100%, and 6,200 members surveyed on arrival in a month is believable for a large leisure centre.
Both pies sum to 100%, and 3,900 exit replies over six weekends at a city botanic garden is believable.
Both pies sum to 100%, and 4,000 interval respondents over a season at a 1,400-seat touring-musical theatre is believable.
A stock-media licensor with $274 million revenue, royalties of 43% and running costs of 36% leaving a 21% operating margin is believable.
A supermarket chiller using about 4,200 to 4,600 kWh a year at 10c/kWh with a few maintenance visits is believable, and the $14 engineer hourly rate is low but within a factor of a few of real rates.
